text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- Bulgaria's Privatisation Agency has invited investment banks to bid to advise the cabinet in the sale of a 25 percent stake of the state-owned Bulgarian Telecommunication Company, the agency's executive director Vesselin Blagoev said.
-- Bulgaria could face difficulties in paying for imports of Russian gas from the beginning of next year, Russia's ambassador to Sofia Alexander Avdeev said.
-- Bulgaria's gross national product is expected to fall by one to two percent by the end of this year in comparision with the end of 1995, deputy prime minister Roumen Gechev said.
-- A big western financial group is offering to buy Bulgaria's private Trade and Savings Bank, which was placed in receivership in September, the newspaper said, without quoting sources.
-- Bulgaria's cumulative inflation is expected to accelerate to 216 percent by the end of this year, higher than the initially expected 105 percent, experts from the International Monetary Fund said.

-- The monthly interest rate on citizens and firms deposits in most commercial banks is set at 16 percent from today in line with the cut of the main interest rate by the central bank from 25 to 20 percent monthly.

-- Bulgaria's cabinet is expected to discuss today an offer by state-owned Bulbank to buy a majority stake in the state Economic Bank, which is in receivership. The central bank disscussed the offer last week.
-- Fuel prices are expected to rise by another 14 percent by the end of October due to the huge losses posted by Bulgaria's largest oil refinery Neftochim, deputy prime minister Roumen Gechev said.
-- Only 14 of the country's 44 commercial banks are in a stable financial condition, said deputy premier Roumen Gechev, citing Expressbank and Bulbank as the country's best state banks.
